slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slot.brief: Electron (or alpha particle) accelerated through a given potential difference; compute its de Broglie wavelength directly via λ = h/√(2mqV).

stem: An $\alpha$ particle starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of $100$ V. Calculate its de Broglie wavelength. Take $h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J s, $m_\alpha=6.64\times10^{-27}$ kg and $e=1.60\times10^{-19}$ C.

verdicts.working: The alpha particle has charge 2e, so K = 2eV = 3.20×10^-17 J. Then λ = h/√(2mαK) = 1.02×10^-12 m.

working:
$q=2e$
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_\alpha qV}}$
$=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2(6.64\times10^{-27})(3.20\times10^{-19})(100)}}$
$=1.02\times10^{-12}$ m

Independent check: The alpha particle has charge 2e, so K = 2eV = 3.20×10^-17 J. Then λ = h/√(2mαK) = 1.02×10^-12 m.
solution:
For an $\alpha$ particle, $q=2e$ and $K=qV$. Hence
$$\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_\alpha qV}}=\frac{6.63\times10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2(6.64\times10^{-27})(3.20\times10^{-19})(100)}}=1.02\times10^{-12}\text{ m}.$$
